description: Save a chart as code into the project's Analytics, creating or replacing by name; the app redraws it wherever it is shown, after every solve. set_dashboard puts it on a dashboard; gallery charts need no code. Name the chart by its data with `chart` (a get_results query and how to draw it), e.g. capacity by year, stacked by carrier: {query: {metric: "capacity", by: ["year", "carrier"]}, type: "bar", x: "year", color: "carrier"}. Write `source` only for what a query cannot show; call with neither for the code contract.

chart.description: A chart named by its data: query = get_results arguments; x and color = dimensions in query.by, or "scenario" to compare scenarios in one panel. x "time" with color "year" overlays the years on a time-of-year axis. histogram: hours at each level of the metric; color up to two dimensions.

bins.description: histogram: a bin count (default 10), or the bin edges.

line.description: With x "time": a metric drawn as a line over it, e.g. "demand".

normalize.description: histogram: bin each series as % of its own peak.

strips.description: x "time": up to 2 panels under it: a gallery time chart ("dispatch", {chart, off}) or metric.

name.description: Chart name, unique in the project.

save_anyway.description: Save even though the check fails: only when it fails because the model has no results yet.

source.description: The whole module: `export const reads` and the default chart function.

strips.description: With only name: set a saved chart's strips ([] clears).

name: write_chart
